section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes a single (unnumbered) study of Chinese adolescent girls, reporting that online interpersonal sexual objectification (OISO) negatively relates to intuitive eating via reduced broad conceptualization of beauty and, in sequence, lower body appreciation. The authors emphasize implications for school- and family-based interventions to broaden beauty conceptualizations and promote body functionality to support intuitive eating, and note that positive body image may be relatively stable and can buffer against OISO.

section_summary.extract_value: The discussion reports that interpersonal sexual objectification (OISO) among Chinese adolescent girls is indirectly associated with reduced intuitive eating via a narrowed conceptualization of beauty and reduced body appreciation. It highlights that broadening girls' conceptualization of beauty and fostering body appreciation may buffer the negative impact of objectification and suggests school- and parent-based interventions to promote body functionality and acceptance.
section_summary.evidence_source: This study is the first to explore factors influencing intuitive eating among Chinese adolescent girls. The results show an indirect effect of OISO experiences on intuitive eating through broad conceptualization of beauty, and an indirect effect of OISO experiences on intuitive eating through broad conceptualization of beauty and body appreciation.
